title: GPU arrival alignments and procurement hedge notes
content:
Purpose:
Short working notes on synchronizing multi-vendor GPU arrivals, recommended hedging levers, and an arrival-alignment heuristic we can use for Q2–Q4 2026 planning. This is intentionally pragmatic: combine order phasing, customs contingency lanes, and regional staging so Dedicated and Private capacity needs are met while minimizing idle days and avoiding last-minute spot buys.

High-level constraints we need to respect:
- Target utilization: 72–78% across prod pool by region (monthly rolling).
- Minimum deployable buffer: 2 weeks of committed capacity at 75% util target per region (to cover deployments + canary rollouts).
- Budget cadence: quarterly procurement approval windows; some emergency tail spend allowed up to $400k per incident.

Key vendor lead-time observations (empirical distribution from last 18 months):
- Vendor A (OEM direct, e.g., A100-class): median 8 weeks, 90th percentile 15 weeks; customs delays +3–6 business days for EU shipments in peak season.
- Vendor B (reseller, e.g., H100/re-sellers): median 6 weeks, 90th percentile 18 weeks; occasional backfill via cross-dock in US-WEST reduces effective lead by 1 week but costs ~8% premium.
- Vendor C (OEM L4 partners for APAC): median 10 weeks, high variance (90th 22 weeks) due to port congestion.

SKU mix guidance (short notes, not final):
- Baseline recommended split (global capacity planning): heavy general-purpose mix to keep inference flexibility: 40% H100-family, 35% A100/GA100-class, 15% L40S/edge-optimized, 10% reserve/low-power for smaller private deployments.
- Region tilts: APAC +10% L40S relative to baseline; EU tilt +5% H100 for high-throughput customers; US-EAST keep balanced.

Arrival alignment heuristic (working algorithm):
1) For each planned quarter, compute region-level expected token-volume growth and translate to GPU-weeks demand (use model-specific tokens->GPU mapping from capacity model).
2) For each vendor SKU, estimate arrival window [median - sd, 90th percentile + clearance buffer].
3) Phase orders so that no single region has >45% of its quarterly new installs arriving in the same 30-day window (avoid onboarding staffing crunch + AMI churn).
4) If 90th percentile causes >buffer breach, insert a hedge tranche (small order) from alternate vendor/reseller with shorter lead times or commit to short-term retail leases.

Practical example (Q3 2026 planning):
- Required new installs: US-WEST 180 GPU-equivalents, EU-WEST 120, APAC 90.
- Candidate order plan: Vendor B (US) 120 H100 -> staggered shipments: 40 early-July, 40 mid-Aug, 40 late-Sep. Vendor A (EU) 100 A100 -> two shipments: 60 early-Aug, 40 mid-Sep. Vendor C (APAC) 90 L40S -> single shipment scheduled mid-Sep but add 10 GPU hedge via reseller in Aug.
- Outcome: reduces onboarding overlap in Aug (historically our highest churn month due to releases) and keeps EU buffer intact.

Buffer / Hedge levers we are proposing (ordered by cost effectiveness):
- Prefix caching & reservation (software): tune cache TTLs to reduce immediate demand for full capacity during staggered onboarding (very cheap).
- Reseller micro-orders: small lots (10–30 GPUs) with +10–15% cost; use only as hedge tranches if 90th percentile triggers.
- Short-term colocation leases / retail GPUs: expensive but useful for <8 week gaps.
- Cross-region soft bursting: borrow underutilized capacity from lower-peak regions for up to 2 weeks (requires routing and billing adjustments).

Operational checklists (for procurement + SRE handoff):
- Procurement: confirm serials, warranty start date alignment, and customs documentation 6 weeks before ETA.
- SRE/Platform: prepare AMI bake windows aligned to planned arrival batches; schedule canary routes to consume first 10–15% of new batch.
- Finance: confirm FX exposure for APAC orders and apply forward contract if >$250k exposure.
- Logistics: pre-book cross-dock for EU shipments if 90th percentile > median by >20%.

Open questions / items to resolve:
- Should we standardize on a single SKU family per region for operational simplicity, or accept heterogeneity and pay the operational overhead? (tradeoff matrix draft needed)
- Do we commit to a 10% global hedging budget (percentage of quarterly order volume) or keep it flexible per quarter?
- How do we automate the arrival-alignment heuristic into the procurement dashboard (data inputs: region demand curve, vendor lead-time distribution, customs-seasonality multipliers)?

Suggested next steps (short term):
- Snapshot current committed arrivals and run a Monte Carlo 10k sim with new heuristic to project overlap risk metric (assign to Samir).
- Draft small policy doc for 'reseller micro-order' approval thresholds (Lucia).
- Align with Finance on forward FX trigger (Ethan).
- Try a single pilot for Q3: place a 10-unit reseller hedge for APAC to validate lead-time assumption.

Notes to self (scratchpad):
- Keep record of cases where cross-dock reduced effective lead-time — useful for vendor negotiation.
- Slack thread: #infra-gpu-procurement has recent vendor A quote (12/2025) that shows improved lead-time in Q2 2026 windows.
- Add a simple column in the procurement sheet: "arrival-risk-score" combining 90th percentile window / % of quarterly installs in 30-day window.

Meeting log (2026-03-09 sync):
- Samir: emphasized need for canary bandwidth when onboarding >50 GPUs in a week.
- Lucia: finance will allow up to 5% reserve hedging without exec sign-off; above that needs CPO ok.
- Ethan: suggested building a small automation to scrape vendor ETAs monthly.

TODOs (owner tags inline):
- [Samir] Run Monte Carlo overlap sim and push results to /infra/procurement/dashboards by 2026-03-24.
- [Lucia] Draft reseller micro-order approval flow and threshold, due 2026-03-20.
- [Ethan] Confirm FX forward trigger and share with procurement by 2026-03-18.
- [Avery] Bake arrival-risk-score into procurement sheet and surface as column.

Bottom line (working):
We should move from single-batch quarterly ordering -> phased, risk-aware batches with explicit micro-hedges and better customs/reseller playbooks. This reduces onboarding spikes and gives SRE/Platform predictable windows for canaries and AMI rollouts, at modest incremental cost compared to emergency spot buys.

End of notes.
